recall.minute: Dependency grammar replaces phrase boxes with head → dependent labelled arcs (solar-system analogy); it suits free word order (Hindi Ram-ne Sita-ko kitaab di) and turns PP attachment into one arc (saw → with vs girl → with in 'I saw a girl with a telescope': nsubj, dobj, det, prep, pobj). Trees are connected, acyclic, single-headed, usually projective. UD standardises relations (nsubj, obj, iobj, amod, det, obl:tmod). Four parser families: DP (Eisner O(n³)), constraint satisfaction, transition-based, graph-based. Arc-eager: c = (S, B, A); SH, LA (buffer → stack top, pop), RA (stack top → buffer, push), RE (pop). 'He sent her a letter .': SH, LA(SBJ), RA(ROOT), RA(IOBJ), RE, SH, LA(DET), RA(DOBJ), RE, RA(PUNC). Oracle trained from treebank-derived actions with features (POS of stack top/buffer front); perceptron w += f(c, t_o) − f(c, t*) (worked: SH [5,6,5] = 6.0 vs LA [5.5,4.5,5.5] = 4.5). O(n), but errors cascade. Graph-based: MST over arc scores; Chu-Liu-Edmonds: best incoming arcs, contract cycle (John↔saw, 50), rescore (root→C 40, Mary→C 31), recurse, unpack → root→saw, saw→John, saw→Mary = 70; global updates w += f(G_true) − f(G').
